content: Elvitegravir is a sensitive substrate of the CYP3A4 enzyme. Co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to the potential for significant drug interactions. Lopinavir, when co-administered, increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. Lorlatenib decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases losartan levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Additionally, it decreases losartan levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Elvitegravir is a moderate inducer of CYP2C9. Cobicistat, a CYP3A4 inhibitor, is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates that have elevated plasma concentrations associated with serious or life-threatening events. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases lovastatin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Cobicistat inhibits CYP3A4 and is contraindicated with substrates of this enzyme that may lead to serious or life-threatening events due to elevated plasma concentrations. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases lumacaftor/ivacaftor levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. No dose adjustment is necessary when CYP3A inhibitors are initiated in patients already on lumacaftor/ivacaftor. However, when starting lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients on strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose to one tablet daily for the first week to allow for steady-state induction effects of lumacaftor. After this period, resume the recommended daily dose. No dose adjustment is required for moderate or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases lurasidone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases macitentan levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Magnesium oxide decreases elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration from antacids by at least two hours. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases maprotiline levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Cobicistat inhibits CYP2D6, and caution is required with substrates of this enzyme that may lead to serious or life-threatening events due to elevated plasma concentrations. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases maraviroc levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be administered with other antiretrovirals. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases mavacamten levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to mavacamten, potentially leading to heart failure due to systolic dysfunction. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases mavorixafor levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Monitor mavorixafor levels if co-administered with P-gp inhibitors and reduce the dose if necessary. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases meclofenamate levels by decreasing renal clearance. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Toxicity may result from co-administration of emtricitabine and tenofovir with other drugs primarily excreted by glomerular filtration or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases medroxyprogesterone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases methadone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases methamphetamine levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Methotrexate and elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Methoxyflurane and elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases methylergonovine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases methylprednisolone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases metoprolol levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases mexiletine levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases midazolam levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated for oral midazolam. For parenteral midazolam, consider dose reduction. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases midostaurin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, monitor midostaurin for increased risk of adverse reactions, especially during the first week of treatment. Mifepristone increases elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases mirtazapine levels by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases mirvetuximab soravtansine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase unconjugated DM4 exposure, raising the risk of adverse reactions. Monitor closely. Mitotane decreases elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; monitor for possible dosage adjustments when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases modafinil levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases mometasone levels (inhaled and intranasal) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to an increased risk of systemic corticosteroid side effects. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases montelukast levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and decreases montelukast levels by altering CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Elvitegravir is a moderate CYP2C9 inducer.
